Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Photovoltaic Cells Achieve 33% Efficiency Record

Author: Claire Chen | September 5, 2025

Photovoltaic Breakthrough in Solar Energy

Researchers at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory have certified a new world-record power conversion efficiency of 33.2% for a monolithic perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell. By absorbing the blue portion of the solar spectrum in the top perovskite layer while transmitting infrared wavelengths to the bottom crystalline silicon wafer, the tandem device overcomes the theoretical Shockley-Queisser single-junction efficiency limit of 29.4%.

Accelerated damp-heat environmental testing demonstrated that encapsulation with ethylene vinyl acetate and butyl rubber edge sealants preserved 95% of initial power output after 1,500 hours under continuous illumination at 85 degrees Celsius and 85% relative humidity. Commercial rooftop solar deployment is expected to begin in early 2027.
